gap: No result ChatGPT got states that "25W" is not one tier: Anker's own page for the Prime 3-in-1 caps iPhone 16 and 16 Pro at 22W and iPhone Air at 20W and excludes iPhone 16e, Apple puts iPhone 17e in the 15W group, and the three makers' case limits differ (ESR under 2 mm, Anker 2.5 mm, Belkin 5 mm).
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best-MagSafe roundup, its ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1, ESR Foldable and Ugreen MagFlow Pro 3-in-1 reviews, and iThinkDiff's 3-in-1 list. Macworld gives only a two-way split ("iPhone 16 and later" 25W, iPhone 12-15 15W), and iThinkDiff gives no per-model wattage. None mentions the 22W/22.5W, 20W, iPhone 17e or iPhone 16e cells, case thickness, or which AirPods and Watch models each maker lists. The Digital Camera World Anker review came back truncated and techgearden.com failed with a certificate error, so those two cited pages were not compared.
decides: It does not change the ESR-first order for iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17, 17 Pro and 18 Pro owners, since all three stations are Qi2.2 25W and those phones take the full 25W. It does decide two sub-cases. For an iPhone 16e, ESR is the only one of the three whose maker lists it (with a magnetic case under 2 mm); Anker says not compatible and Belkin's list omits it. For a thick case, Belkin's 5 mm allowance beats Anker's 2.5 mm and ESR's under 2 mm. It also corrects ChatGPT's closing line: iPhone 17e is a 15W phone, and iPhone 16, 16 Pro and Air peak below 25W.

findings.label: Apple's iPhone wireless power tiers (Apple MagSafe Charger)
findings.value: Up to 25W: iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, 17, 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max. iPhone 16 and 16 Pro: 22.5W peak. iPhone Air: 20W peak. iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier: up to 15W; iPhone 13 mini and 12 mini up to 12W. The 25W tier needs a 30W or greater adapter at 15V/2.0A or higher.
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Page published 2026-09-18. It describes Apple's own MagSafe Charger (A3502, A3503, A2580, A3250) and does not mention Qi2 25W third-party chargers; Anker's page above states matching 22W and 20W caps for its own station. The page calls iPhone 16e and iPhone 11 "non-MagSafe Qi-compatible devices".

findings.label: Apple on heat while wirelessly charging

findings.label: Which Apple Watch models fast charge
findings.value: Series 7 and later, SE 3, and Ultra and later. 0-80% in about 30 minutes for Series 10 and later; about 45 minutes for Series 7-9, SE 3 and Ultra 3 and later; about an hour for Ultra and Ultra 2.
findings.source_title: About fast charge on Apple Watch - Apple Support
findings.note: Page published 2026-09-17. Apple says fast charging requires an Apple USB-C Magnetic Fast Charging Cable and that WPT-compliant chargers do not support fast charging. Series 6 and earlier and SE 1/2 are outside the list, so they charge at standard speed on any of the three stations.
